line: Ray Treviño. Treviño Insurance, on Grand next to the bakery. I pay for the softball team's uniforms, so Pilar lets me say hello. Ray, not Ramón. Only my mother says Ramón.
I came from Monterrey at nine. First week of school, the teacher said 'Raymond' and I said yes. Best decision I ever made, and I didn't even make it.
For what? My kids are Tyler and Megan. No Spanish. My kids won't need any of this, and that's fine. They need a good credit score and a firm handshake.
You can't miss what you never had. My mother says I took something from them. I say I took the accent off the phone. Thirty years I've sold policies on the phone.
The softball team lost twelve to two on Sunday. The uniforms looked great. I paid for the uniforms. My job is done.
choice2: Twelve to two is a lot.

line: Open enrollment. Your HR hired me to explain the dental plan to people who won't read it. Short version? Take the one with the cleanings.
choice1: The one with the cleanings. Got it.

line: You've got a good way with people. A tip from a guy who learned the hard way: on a résumé, the hall goes under 'Community,' not 'Cultural.' Same thing. Reads different.
Chamber of Commerce breakfast, Thursday, seven a.m. Bankers, a dentist, Frank from the hardware store. I want to bring someone young who gets it. That's you.
Half my clients called this week asking if their policy asks about status. It doesn't. I tell them: pay on time, drive the limit, be boring. Boring is safe.
The state is putting insurance forms out in Spanish. Fine. I'll keep sending mine in English. People learn faster when they have to.
choice1: Or they sign things they can't read.

line: Every time I come to the hall, you're here. Good people. But don't spend every Saturday in one building. The city's bigger than Grand Avenue.
Frank DeLuca says he sees you around Fifth. Good. That's how it works. Five years from now, nobody asks where you started.
Can't stop, I've got a client at ten about a hail claim. Hail! In October.
